title: Even unimodular ideal lattices of rank 88 over Q(zeta_115): note, addenda, data, programs and verifications (version 1.5.1: prior-work corrections)
description:
Note, addenda, data, programs and verification records on even unimodular ideal lattices of rank 88 over the cyclotomic field L = Q(zeta_115). The note is given in English (article/rang88_en.pdf, a translation) and in its original French (article/rang88.pdf).

Note. The set S of classes of unimodular ideal lattices over L is in bijection with the class group of L (a consequence of a result of Bayer-Fluckiger, 1984, since h-(115) is odd and h(L+) = 1; the note gives a direct proof for m = 115), which is cyclic of order h-(115) = 44 697 909 (a tabulated value, OEIS A061653); it splits into 508 463 Galois orbits. Sakamoto's two extremal lattices lie in the principal orbit and in the unique non-trivial 3-torsion orbit. Two ideal lattices over L with minimum at least 8 are isometric if and only if their classes are Galois conjugate. The direction "conjugate, hence isometric" is classical (used in the proof of Cor. 3.3 of Bayer-Fluckiger 1984; stated in Sect. 5 of Bayer-Fluckiger and Suarez 2005 and in Lemma 4.3 b) of Nebe 2016, arXiv 1409.8473v1); the converse direction extends an argument of Quebbemann (J. reine angew. Math. 326, 1981) for automorphisms of prime order. In dimensions 48 and 72, Nebe (2013, 2016) has classified the extremal ideal lattices over cyclotomic fields, composite conductors included; in these cases the extremal lattices form a single isometry class, and we found there neither a statement nor a general argument for the direction "isometric, hence conjugate" (for m = 65 it follows from a remark in the proof of Nebe 2013, Thm. 5.3, and from Step 3 of the proof of the isometry theorem). A gluing construction is extended to non-principal ideals, and a finite extremality criterion is derived from a Parseval-type inequality (the idea of bounding a minimum from below by a Parseval identity is also in Quebbemann 1981, p. 168). The orbits of eight prime ideals are rejected by explicit vectors of norm 6. For two prime ideals of degree 2, above 139 and 599, the lattices X139 and X599 are extremal: their minimum 8 is established by a computer-assisted proof, with an explicit execution model, and the computations were replicated on a second computer. Without assuming GRH, they are isometric neither to Sakamoto's lattices nor, under this computer-assisted minimum, to each other.

Addendum (version 1.1). Two further extremal lattices, X4969 and X4049 (computer-assisted minimum, each side swept twice on two rented machines with byte-identical receipts); extremality is not an invariant of the twin pairs of the sigma24 layer; a description of the orbits of that layer without GRH.

Version 1.2. Norm-6 witnesses of the rejections in the addendum, with two checkers written in different languages (PARI/GP and pure Python).

Version 1.3. English translation of the note and updated French text (status of the non-isometry without GRH; normalizers of the multiplication group of orders 460 and 920 in Aut(X139) and Aut(X599)); archive metadata. No new computation.

Version 1.4. Timestamped data for two further even unimodular ideal lattices of rank 88, attached to products of two primes of degree 1 swapped by a Galois automorphism (folder v14_P1151s24_et_candidat_P461s91/): one extremal lattice and one CANDIDATE. X(P1151sigma24), with I = (1151, zeta - 6)(1151, zeta - 605): computer-assisted minimum 8 (exhaustive sweep of both sides of the criterion, no touch), run twice on two different machines with identical canonical fingerprints of the receipts; its class is not Galois conjugate to those of the six known extremal lattices, without assuming GRH. X(P461sigma91), a CANDIDATE, with I = (461, zeta - 5)(461, zeta - 115): exhaustive sweep of both sides without touch on a single machine, not replicated (one side resumed from an interrupted launch; only the short part of the receipts is cross-checked, against those of P461sigma24); minimum 8 claimed by the author; non-isometric to X139, X599, X4969, X4049, X(P1151sigma24) and LS without assuming GRH, and to L0 only under GRH. The note and the addendum are unchanged. (Both reservations on X(P461sigma91) are lifted in version 1.5.)

Version 1.5 (Addendum 3). Two further lattices with computer-assisted minimum 8 (folder v15_P3359_et_P461s91/ and addendum3/). X(P3359), with I = (3359, zeta^2 + 2202 zeta + 1829), a prime of degree 2: both sides of the criterion swept without any touch, twice, on two machines, with the same program and receipts identical task by task. X(P461sigma91): a fresh second run reproduces all 146 603 receipts of the run of version 1.4 byte for byte, so it is no longer an unreplicated candidate. A certificate, checked by a program that uses only the Python standard library, shows without GRH (Jacobi sums and Stickelberger's theorem) that the 45013-component of the class of X(P461sigma91) is non-zero; hence it is isometric neither to L0 nor to LS, without GRH and without any computer-assisted step on our side. A second implementation of the criterion gives a numerical cross-check on X(P461sigma91) (not a certificate; no run on X(P3359) had been completed as of November 7, 2026). Under the stated hypotheses, at least nine pairwise non-isometric extremal lattices of rank 88 are known. The note and the addendum are corrected: citation of Quebbemann (1981), whose argument the isometry theorem extends, and of Bayer-Fluckiger (1984, Cor. 3.3, an upper bound); the non-isometry between two lattices requires the computer-assisted minimum 8 of one of them, except with respect to L0 and LS. All corrections are listed in CHANGEMENTS_V15.md.

Version 1.5.1 (November 8, 14 and 23, 2026). Prior-work corrections to the note and to Addendum 3, with no additional computation; no mathematical statement, data or program is changed, and the numbering of statements is unchanged; the proof of Thm. 3.3 only gains a reference to Bayer-Fluckiger and Suarez (2005). The note now describes Nebe's classifications by enumeration of the extremal ideal lattices of dimensions 48 and 72, composite conductors included (2013, Thm. 5.3 of arXiv 1212.0865v1, numbered 5.5 in the author's final file; 2016, Thm. 4.5 of arXiv 1409.8473v1), and claims only the direction "isometric, hence conjugate" of the isometry theorem. The bijection between S and the class group follows from Bayer-Fluckiger (1984, Prop. 3.1 and Lemma 3.2 a)); the value h-(115) is tabulated (OEIS A061653); the direction "conjugate, hence isometric" is referred to the proof of Cor. 3.3 of Bayer-Fluckiger (1984) and to Sect. 5 of Bayer-Fluckiger and Suarez (J. Number Theory 114, 2005), which states it explicitly. One more published composite case (Quebbemann 1992, m = 68, dimension 32) was not read. These corrections were prepared with Claude Opus 5.5 and have not been reviewed by a specialist. All corrections are listed in CHANGEMENTS_V151.md.

Status: the minimum 8 of the lattices found by the author is computer-assisted (execution model M1, M2, H1-H3 stated in the note); it is not a formal proof. It rests on a single program, run on two machines for each lattice, and has not been audited by a human. Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) and Astra (OpenAI) assisted the author; they are not authors.
